fe9af2101aaddbb9: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — An abandoned shopping mall, a mysterious faceless entity, and a game that takes a terrifying turn set the stage for Kacau, with the upcoming horror thriller unveiling its official trailer and poster ahead of its cinema release on November 12.
Directed by Muzzamer Rahman, whose previous work includes Prebet Sapu, the film is adapted from Ariff Adly’s bestselling novel published by Buku Fixi.
The trailer and poster were first unveiled on October 12 and released on social media on October 13.
Designed by Lah Hamid, the poster features a faceless entity towering over the film’s seven main characters, hinting at the supernatural threat that awaits them.
The characters are portrayed by Evanatie Sannie, Sadiq M. Jamil, Fimie Don, Idan Aedan, Khayrisyah Kemal, Arfie Shah, and Nurel Baharin.
Meanwhile, the trailer gives audiences a closer look at the film’s unsettling atmosphere, with an abandoned shopping mall serving as the setting for the unfolding horror.
It also teases the faceless entity’s appearance, scenes of characters coming under attack, and the Spirit of the Coin game that sets the terrifying events in motion.
Set to hit cinemas nationwide on November 12, 2026, Kacau has secured 80 screening locations across the country.

The production team hopes for strong audience support during the film’s first four days in cinemas, as the initial response will be crucial in determining whether it continues its run into the following week.
Director Muzzamer also shared that although author Ariff was not involved in technical filmmaking aspects, such as camera movements, his influence on the film was 100 per cent.
At its heart, Kacau follows a group of young friends whose attempt to play Spirit of the Coin leads them into an encounter with a supernatural entity.
What begins as a ghost-hunting adventure soon turns into a fight to survive as the haunting takes a frightening turn.
With its eerie setting and mysterious antagonist, the film looks to bring a new dose of supernatural suspense to local cinema audiences this November.
abf421020aee5df3: MIRI, Oct 14 — A 16-year-old student was killed after being struck by a car while crossing the road near SMK Luar Bandar Miri in Bekenu on Tuesday.

Miri police chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said the accident occurred at about 1.10pm when a car driven by a 46-year-old local woman, travelling from Miri towards Bakong, allegedly struck the student.
“The student was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical assistant from Tun Abang Haji Openg Bekenu Health Clinic,” he said in a statement on Tuesday night.
Mohd Farhan said the impact damaged the front-left section of the car, while the driver was unhurt.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.

Meanwhile police have urged anyone with information about the accident to contact investigating officer Insp Mohd Faizal Moktar at 012-818 6509 or 085-430479, or report to the nearest police station. — The Borneo Post
766957f1d804b8f6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government has settled tax overpayment refunds amounting to RM17.15 billion, involving 3.23 million taxpayer cases, for the period up to September 30, 2026.

According to the Ministry of Finance (MoF), this total included RM6.38 billion being refunded to 3.1 million individual taxpayers and RM8.95 billion being refunded to over 130,000 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

To strengthen the processing of tax refunds, the Inland Revenue Board has implemented various strategies that are fairer and more equitable, ensuring that refund allocations from the government are distributed in an orderly and effective manner based on the age of outstanding cases, while also prioritising MSMEs and companies facing cash flow issues.

“The government is also committed to ensuring that outstanding refunds are fully settled promptly as part of efforts to enhance tax administration efficiency and safeguard taxpayers' rights, in line with the Madani government’s fiscal reform agenda,” the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said in a written reply published on the parliament website yesterday.

The ministry was replying to a question from Lim Guan Eng (Bagan-PH) regarding the timeframe for settling excess tax refunds and the two per cent compensation for corporate taxpayers for the 2025 year of assessment, as well as the amount of outstanding refunds according to the year of assessment and the number of affected taxpayers. — Bernama

0498eb5f98644507: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The increased interim special grants and larger development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak are expected to strengthen development in both states, with Members of Parliament (MPs) hoping this will be followed by a finalised special grant formula and more effective project implementation.

Debating the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, Datuk Seri Doris Sophia Brodi (GPS-Sri Aman) said the increase in the interim special grant for both states from RM600 million to RM1.5 billion should be appreciated.

However, she hoped the federal government would expedite the drafting of a final formula that is transparent, objective and sustainable under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution and in line with the spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).

Datuk Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar (BN-Kinabatangan) urged the government to explain the latest status of negotiations on the formula granting Sabah the right to receive 40 per cent of the net revenue derived by the Federal Government from the state.
“This is not just a matter of additional allocations; it involves constitutional responsibility and fiscal relations between the federal government and the Sabah government.

“Therefore, I ask the government to clarify the latest status of the 40 per cent formula negotiations, the method for verifying the federal net revenue derived from Sabah and the targeted timeline to reach a solution with the state government,” he said.
Meanwhile, Datuk Wetrom Bahanda (KDM-Kota Marudu) proposed that unspent development allocations for Sabah be carried forward to the following year by establishing a Carry Forward Fund.
He said the mechanism would ensure approved allocations continue to be utilised, especially when project implementation faces bureaucratic, technical or other constraints that cause delays.

Wetrom noted that Sabah received an allocation of RM18.7 billion for 2027, an increase of RM1.1 billion from the previous year, but failing to use the entire sum would be detrimental to a state still in need of basic infrastructure development.

Echoing Wetrom’s sentiments, Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau (GRS-Tuaran) urged the Federal Government to end the culture of announcing development projects that ultimately get delayed and become “sick” projects.
Madius also called for measures to ensure Sabah’s development allocations are fully spent to benefit the people.

He asked the government to detail the amount of Sabah’s 2026 development allocation that had been disbursed and spent, including the value of projects implemented by the Sabah Public Works Department (JKR) and the number of sick projects in the state managed by both Sabah JKR and Federal JKR.

He also proposed five improvement measures, including ensuring land, approval and utility matters are resolved before a project begins, and publicly disclosing physical progress, actual expenditure, completion dates and any extensions of time for projects.

“Sick projects must also have recovery plans and follow-up actions. A second extension of time due to contractor weaknesses should undergo an independent review, including considering contract termination in accordance with the law.
“Additionally, Sabah JKR should be empowered as the technical agency for federal projects valued at RM50 million and below,” he said.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting continues today. — Bernama
567d9988a3bb2c2e: TOKYO:The dollar languished on Wednesday as traders awaited fresh signals on the timing of interest rate hikes to contend with persistent inflation.
The greenback weakened from an 18-month high in the previous session as oil prices eased and investors reassessed the AI-fuelled rally that has supported demand for US assets.
The euro clung to gains as budget concerns in France kept regional bond yields elevated and markets on edge.
Attention now focuses on the release of US consumer price index data as well as speeches from Federal Reserve policymakers that could clarify the outlook for interest rates.

"The risk is the core CPI surprises to the upside because of strong consumer demand and higher costs, pushing up market pricing of an October Fed hike and the USD," Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said in a note.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged 0.02 per cent lower to 102.16, following a 0.35 per cent slide on Tuesday. The euro rose 0.04 per cent to US$1.1203.
The yen was little changed at 158.32 per dollar, and sterling rose 0.03 per cent to US$1.3256.
The dollar extended losses on Tuesday after New York Fed President John Williams said he still expects one more rate hike this year, but sees no need for further increases in 2027.

The US Labor Department is due to release its CPI for September, which is expected to have risen 0.60 per cent month-on-month after increasing 0.40 per cent in August, while annual inflation is seen accelerating to 3.60 per cent from 3.40 per cent. Additionally, the Fed is due to publish its Beige Book.

Traders see a 77 per cent chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 51 per cent a month ago, while pricing in about 75 basis points of tightening by late 2027, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.

Investors abandoned bets on a Fed rate hike later this month after two policymakers argued for gathering more evidence before deciding whether further tightening is needed, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller said inflation expectations remained "well anchored".

Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin is scheduled to participate in a fireside chat in Virginia, while Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman is set to take part in talks in Bangkok.
The International Monetary Fund and World Bank's annual meetings continue in Bangkok, with several appearances expected by European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde on Wednesday.
The Australian dollar strengthened 0.06 per cent against the greenback to US$0.6984, while New Zealand's kiwi strengthened 0.09 per cent to US$0.5614.
f147e208e01ba9fa: IPOH: The Perak state government has assured that the state's domestic, industrial and agricultural water needs will be prioritised before any surplus is supplied to Penang under the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA).

Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the approach was crucial to ensuring a sustainable water supply in the state, particularly in anticipation of rising demand in the years ahead.
"Whether for domestic consumption, industrial use or padI cultivation, we will prioritise Perak's water needs, with demand estimated at 1,500 million litres per day.
"We will consider supplying water to Penang only if there is a surplus after meeting Perak's domestic, industrial and agricultural requirements," he told Bernama.

He was commenting on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement during the tabling of Budget 2027 that the Madani government had facilitated a 40-year BWSA between the Perak and Penang state governments.
The agreement, signed between Khazanah Air Perak Sdn Bhd (KAP) and Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP), targets the initial delivery of treated water in the first quarter of 2032.

Nizar said the project would also support the development of the Kerian Integrated Green Industrial Park (KIGIP), which is emerging as a key destination for new investments, particularly in the digital sector.

"KIGIP is benefiting from the spillover of the digital industry from Penang. The assurance of a reliable water supply will give investors greater confidence to establish and expand their businesses in Perak," he said.

He added that a stable water supply would also help address supply disruptions in the Kamunting industrial area and at Tasik Bukit Merah in Kerian, an important water source for agricultural and domestic use.
The large-scale project would also generate additional revenue for KAP, create job opportunities and enable more systematic management of water levels at Tasik Bukit Merah, he said.

"Local communities, particularly padifarmers and inland fishermen around Tasik Bukit Merah, will also benefit from better management of the lake's water levels, which could help reduce the risk of drought," he said.
7ad47684fdb8cd7a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Young people aged 30 and below recorded 65.9 million Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) transactions worth RM5.4 billion in the first half of 2026, accounting for 37.9 per cent of total BNPL transactions in Malaysia, according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF).

In a written reply published on the parliament website yesterday, the MoF said the total number of BNPL transactions in Malaysia during that period was 173.9 million, valued at RM14.7 billion, with youths contributing 36.7 per cent of the total transaction value.

As of June 30, 2026, the outstanding BNPL financing balance for this demographic stood at RM2.4 billion, while non-performing financing amounted to RM96.8 million, or 4.0 per cent of the outstanding balance.

The MoF was replying to a question from Datuk Dr Alias Razak (Kuala Nerus-PN) regarding measures taken by the Consumer Credit Commission to protect young people from excessive indebtedness through BNPL schemes, including the comprehensive assessment of consumers’ credit commitments. — Bernama
23b4a5bc0590d915: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The seasoned fish eggs commonly served on sushi rolls are culinary garnishes rather than luxury caviar substitutes under customs law, the High Court has ruled.

Judge Norliza Othman dismissed an appeal by the Customs Department director-general against a Customs Appeal Tribunal decision that favoured restaurant chain Sushi King Sdn Bhd regarding the classification of imported tobiko (flying fish roe), masago (capelin roe), and frozen mentaiko (pollock roe), NST reported.
The decision confirms that the three products attract zero import duty as prepared or preserved fish, sparing the restaurant operator an 8 per cent tariff imposed on caviar substitutes.

Customs argued that cleaning, seasoning, colouring, and freezing the roe qualified them as caviar substitutes under the Customs Duties Order 2017, contending that consumption methods should not influence tariff classifications.
Sushi King maintained that the roe was imported exclusively as garnishes in Japanese dining and was never marketed or consumed as an alternative to sturgeon caviar.
Norliza agreed, holding that preparation methods alone do not transform everyday fish eggs into a luxury caviar alternative.
“Fish roe is a wide, all-encompassing term used to describe fish eggs, but not all fish roe is caviar or a caviar substitute.

“In this regard, caviar substitute is a very specific subset of fish roe based on its origin, methods of consumption and method of processing, which aims to mimic sturgeon caviar,” she said in written grounds published yesterday.

Citing World Customs Organisation guidelines, the judge held that caviar substitutes must be prepared and consumed in the manner of caviar, concluding that the tribunal had properly assessed the culinary reality of the products before setting aside the department’s tariff rulings.
0073c1ea0b1c58e5: TOKYO:Oil prices climbed on Wednesday as traders weighed supply risks from fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and Saudi Arabia against the prospect of increased diesel exports from Russia.

Brent crude futures rose 89 cents, or eight-tenths of a per cent, to US$106.58 a barrel by 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 80 cents, or nine-tenths of a per cent, to US$94.94. Brent fell 0.9 per cent on Tuesday, while WTI rose 0.4 per cent.

"Supply concern stemming from conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is driving prices higher," said chief strategist Hiroyuki Kikukawa at Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities.

"However, the expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement in either direction," Kikukawa said, projecting WTI to trade between US$90 and US$100 a barrel.
The Houthis attacked an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Wednesday.

The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in retaliation for the kingdom's support of Yemeni government forces. Riyadh's international airport has been hit four times, with a strike on Saturday killing 13 people.

Last month, Saudi Arabia raised oil production despite disruption to shipments caused by the US-Iran war, leading to a sharp production increase from OPEC+ — the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and partners, including Russia — OPEC said on Tuesday.
Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships in the Strait of Hormuz to keep oil prices high and influence US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.
In Russia, the government said on Tuesday it did not see any direct link between peace talks with Ukraine and its deal to export diesel to the US.
The comment came after Reuters reported that US envoys had told Ukrainian officials on Friday that the deal was part of an attempt to draw Russia back to negotiations for a peace settlement.
a4b208c9b12a8d5e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The adoption of technology and business scaling can boost company productivity and enhance the ability to share the gains of growth with employees through wage increases, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He noted that efforts to raise productivity to support wage growth must involve not only employees but also the capabilities of employers.

“The current wage increases must be balanced with productivity, not only at the level of the workers themselves but also among employers,” he told Bernama after appearing as a guest on the Bernama TV programme Ruang Bicara, titled “Budget 2027: Quality Economic Growth, Prosperous People” yesterday evening.
Akmal Nasrullah said the adoption of technology and financing that supports business scaling are among the ways to strengthen the capabilities of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
“When we speak of the capabilities of MSMEs, we certainly hope they will continue to strengthen their businesses.
“As that scaling-up occurs more effectively and comprehensively, they will be able to share a portion of the growth proceeds with their workers,” he said.

Regarding the sectors targeted for productivity improvements to support wage increases, he said the manufacturing sector needs to move towards more comprehensive technology adoption, rather than relying on low-cost labour, including foreign workers.
He said the initiative aligns with the 13th Malaysia Plan target of reducing reliance on foreign workers from 15 per cent to 10 per cent by the end of the plan period.
“Such sectors certainly need continued encouragement to further enhance their productivity and capabilities,” he said.
According to Akmal Nasrullah, the use of energy-efficient machinery or equipment is also a method for reducing company operating costs.

He noted that government matching grants are available for conducting energy efficiency audits, while details regarding specific funds for technology adoption and productivity enhancement fall under the purview of the relevant ministries. — Bernama

babcc6ad7c2fc5ed: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government has allocated RM21.26 billion in development expenditure to six underdeveloped states under Budget 2027, with the distribution taking into account the different needs of each state, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.

He said the six states are Kelantan, Terengganu, Perlis, Kedah, Sabah and Sarawak, with the allocation also reflecting the commitment to infrastructure development and the implementation of previously announced projects.

“There are states that, in terms of infrastructure development for the period we announced, may require a significant commitment. At the same time, this also involves projects that, although not announced this year, will commence implementation this year,” he told Bernama.
He said this after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme, titled “Budget 2027: Quality Economic Growth, Prosperous People,” last night.
Akmal Nasrullah said development spending is not only aimed at driving economic growth but also at bridging the development gap between states, including those that are lagging behind.

He said the commitment and allocation for the six states, as stated in the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), would continue regardless of political differences, in line with the responsibilities of the federal government.

Regarding development spending priorities, Akmal Nasrullah said that, of the total RM83 billion allocated for development under Budget 2027, the focus includes infrastructure development, the creation of economic opportunities and the enhancement of social mobility.

He noted that the development of schools and healthcare facilities, as well as efforts to address the impacts of climate change, are also priorities to ensure that spending delivers high-impact outcomes.
Among the examples given was the commitment to develop a dam in Kelantan to address flooding, as well as steps towards constructing a water treatment plant in Machang.

Earlier in the Ruang Bicara programme, he said the Ministry of Economy evaluates development expenditure based on the desired outcomes to ensure that project implementation achieves the intended objectives.

“Sometimes, for example, when implementing a programme or project, even if the project is completed, it can become a white elephant because the planning may have been driven by certain urgent needs. The project is then carried out, but in terms of achieving the objectives we had intended, it does not get very far,” he said.
He said the risks of delays, such as those involving land acquisition and utility relocation, need to be managed more carefully and comprehensively, but these issues should not be used as excuses.

Akmal Nasrullah said the ministry is now evaluating the implementation of preliminary studies before allowing full project applications to proceed, to avoid situations in which issues such as site incompatibility are identified only after a project has been announced.

“If the construction process takes around three years, but the initial phase of identifying the site and so on takes two years, in my opinion, this means the public have to wait an unreasonable length of time for the infrastructure to become available for their use,” he added. — Bernama
f85c6866af4d5509: KUALA LUMPUR: An average of 24 bullying cases were recorded daily in schools between March and August this year, bringing the total to 4,289 cases over six months.

Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the cases, including incidents in hostels, comprised 2,480 involving physical bullying, 1,386 verbal bullying, 243 non-verbal bullying and 180 cyberbullying.
In response, she said, the Education Ministry has stepped up hostel monitoring through expanded closed-circuit television (CCTV) coverage, additional assistant wardens and safety audits.
CCTV cameras were installed in 200 boarding schools in 2025 and another 333 schools this year, with allocations of RM3 million and RM5 million respectively.
Another RM15 million has been allocated for 2027 to expand CCTV coverage to 1,000 schools nationwide.
Fadhlina said 300 MyStep Hostel Assistant Warden Personnel (MyPWA) had been deployed since April to support more than 10,000 existing wardens, particularly in strengthening night-time supervision.

The ministry had also audited hostel safety at 850 schools, with follow-up efforts this year through the Student Safety and Well-being Survey (TKKM) and In-Situ Guidance: Student Safety and Well-being (BKKM).
"Safety monitoring cannot rely solely on physical facilities.

"Supervision by school personnel, awareness of changes in students' behaviour and prompt action on complaints are also important components in ensuring a safe hostel environment," she said in a parliamentary reply.
Fadhlina said the ministry had upgraded its Bullying Complaints Portal to allow anonymous reports, giving students and witnesses a safer channel to lodge complaints.
Bullying cases are managed under the ministry's Circular No. 12 of 2023, while school safety is guided by Circular No. 3 of 2026.

The Anti-Bullying Act 2026, drafted with the Legal Affairs Division, came into force in stages from March 1 and was fully implemented on June 16. It provides for an Anti-Bullying Tribunal through which victims can seek redress.

"The ministry continues to strengthen its comprehensive approach to tackling bullying, covering enforcement, monitoring of school and hostel environments, victim protection, psychosocial intervention and student character development," she said.
Prevention efforts also include the School Anti-Bullying Framework for Empowerment (SAFE), introduced under Budget 2026, which promotes caring school practices, peer support and targeted counselling.

Fadhlina was responding to Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan (PN-Permatang Pauh), who asked about the number of bullying cases since the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 came into force and improvements to hostel monitoring following revelations during the inquest into Zara Qairina's death.
74682675134189ec: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have identified a syndicate and several individuals believed to be linked to the arrests and drug seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport, Laos, earlier this month.

Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators had recorded statements from several witnesses, including a Malaysian who acted as a broker who arranged the charter of the aircraft involved.
He said the aircraft had been chartered by a 54-year-old Filipino man, identified as a former pilot with a drug-related criminal record in his home country.
“Investigations have also revealed the involvement of a 51-year-old Filipino woman who is believed to have acted as the syndicate’s coordinator,” he said in a statement yesterday.

Hussein said the case was being handled by the NCID’s Special Investigation Unit under Sections 34 and 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, relating to abetment or preparation in Malaysia for drug trafficking offences committed abroad.
He said the NCID was also working closely with the Foreign Ministry and the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) to obtain further information and assist in the investigation.

He said the NCID remained committed to combating drugs to protect present and future generations, and urged members of the public with information on drug-related activities to contact the NCID hotline at 012-208 7222.
On October 1, Lao police seized 521 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Subang.

Following the incident, 13 individuals, including Malaysian, Singaporean and Filipino nationals, were detained by Lao authorities to assist in investigations into the cross-border drug smuggling case.
On October 7, police arrested a local man who owned the private jet during a raid at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang. — Bernama
e74e97d35f6e472a: KUALA LUMPUR: Police will send an investigation team to Japan following the arrest of five Malaysians after 5kg of cocaine was found hidden in their shoe insoles at Haneda Airport in Tokyo on Oct 10.

Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team would gather information about the arrests, including details of local and international drug syndicate networks.
He said Japanese authorities were also investigating the source of the cocaine and working to identify syndicate members and international drug trafficking networks.
"Japanese authorities have informed NCID about the arrest of two Malaysian men and three women at Haneda Airport on Oct 10.
"Their customs officers found 5kg of cocaine hidden in the insoles of shoes worn by all five suspects," he said in a statement.
The confirmation clarifies earlier reports that four men and one woman had been arrested in the case.
Hussein said checks on travel records showed that six Malaysians had departed together from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2 for Haneda on Oct 9 for a holiday.
However, only five were detained by Japanese authorities, while the sixth was not arrested and has since returned to Malaysia.
He said NCID had identified all six people, aged between 19 and 26, including the person who had returned to Malaysia.
"Five of them are from Sarawak, and checks showed that none had any previous criminal record," he said.
Hussein advised the public to be wary of holiday offers, particularly those involving requests to carry other people's bags or belongings overseas.
He also urged the public not to accept or carry items without knowing their contents, to avoid being exploited as drug mules.
Anyone with information on drug-related activities can contact the NCID hotline at 012-208 7222.
Japanese media had earlier reported that five Malaysians were arrested after customs officers found cocaine concealed in shoe insoles when they arrived at Haneda Airport.
According to TBS News DIG, each suspect was believed to have been carrying about 1kg of cocaine, with two 500g packages concealed in each shoe.
The report also quoted a suspect as saying that he had been offered payment of RM8,000 per person to transport drugs overseas through the Telegram messaging app.
Japanese media estimated the total value of the seized cocaine around 120 million yen (RM3.1 million).
Meanwhile, Tokyo Reporter, citing a Nippon News Network (NNN) report on Oct 12, claimed that one of the five Malaysians arrested had been detained alongside his wife and several friends.
However, the police have yet to confirm whether two of the suspects are married.

55c618bfa673f9a5: OCTOBER 14 — Two years ago in 2024, I wrote that Petronas is truly Malaysian.
That year in this month, Petronas celebrated its 50th anniversary following the passing of the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (PDA).

Calling the PDA “historic”, the Minister of Primary Industries Abdul Taib bin Mahmud disclosed to Parliament that the Federal Government had “a very long consultation with the State Governments such as Sarawak and Sabah” and offered his heartfelt gratitude to both states as follows:

“On behalf of the Federal Government, I would like to express my gratitude to the Sarawak and Sabah State Governments for their willingness, for the sake of national interest, to cooperate with the Federal Government.... I reckon that Honourable members will agree that the [passing of the Act] demonstrates the ability and competence of the leaders of the two states.”

Another prominent Sarawakian, Abdul Rahman bin Ya’kub, who was the first to rise during the parliamentary debate to support the legislation, explained the support of the East Malaysian states as follows:
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
File picture of the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur. ― Picture by Choo Choy May

“There is no doubt that the time has come for our country Malaysia to take one very important step that can guarantee that the exploration and exploitation of petroleum will not be dominated and controlled, but also given the highest attention by the Government.

“Petroleum, which is so important to the country, should not be a matter of contention between the states in the federation, it must be considered of national interest. It is for this reason that the State Government of Sarawak and the Government of Sabah have agreed with the Federal Government that [the legislation] be [before] this House.”

As I wrote in 2024, Petronas, through its wholly owned Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd, recorded 19 exploration discoveries over the course of 2023. The discoveries, made from drilling 25 wells, contributed more than 1 billion barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) of new resources.
BOE is used to summarise the amount of energy that is equivalent to the amount of energy found in a barrel of crude oil.
More than half of the discoveries were made in the Sarawak basin.

In that year (2023), the national oil and gas company’s total capital investments (Capex) amounted to RM52.8 billion, mainly attributed to upstream and gas projects. Domestic Capex increased by 41 per cent against the year before mainly for investments in Sabah and Sarawak.
In 2024, Capex increased to RM54.2 billion, with more than 60 per cent of it being invested directly into Malaysian projects, marking a 27 per cent increase in domestic spending compared to 2023.
In 2025, Capex decreased but still stood at RM41.6 billion, mainly from upstream development and production activities.

Based on the Capex in Malaysian projects alone, including in Sarawak, it makes sense that Petronas should file a petition at the Federal Court to seek clarity on the applicable regulatory framework governing its operations in Sarawak. The respondents are the Federal Government and State Government of Sarawak.
Legal clarity is needed on Petronas’ operations in Sarawak, to ensure that the company continues to operate in full compliance with the applicable laws and sound governance practices.

Petronas said it in clear terms that the legal action is not intended to challenge Sarawak’s development aspirations or hinder the role of Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (Petros) in the state’s energy sector.
The legal action followed constructive engagements since 2024 with Petros and both the Federal and State Governments through a series of dialogues and negotiations.

While progress has been made on many commercial arrangements and partnerships – including the signing of Commercial Settlement Agreement (CSA) in 2020 – there have been differences which led to uncertainty in respect of the obligations applicable to Petronas.
The Sarawak Government in turn has filed its own petition at the same court to challenge three federal laws, intending to oppose Petronas’ petition for legal clarity.

Deputy minister in the Sarawak premier’s department Sharifah Hasidah Sayeed Aman Ghazali said the petition sought to determine the constitutional validity and continued applicability of the three laws – that is, the PDA, the Continental Shelf Act 1966 (CSA) and the Petroleum Mining Act 1966 (PMA).

“These federal Acts adversely affect and deprive the rights of Sarawak to the natural resources, including oil and gas, found in the seabed of the continental shelf within the boundaries as defined by the Sarawak Order in Council 1954 and the Sarawak Order in Council 1958,” Sharifah Hasidah said.
Read here on Order in Council and here on laws passed before Malaysia Day.

“Sarawak is justified in safeguarding the legitimate interests and rights of Sarawak and its people, enshrined in the Federal Constitution as well as in the Malaysia Agreement 1963, by seeking a ruling from the Federal Court on the continuing application and effect of these federal Acts in Sarawak” she added.

It’s kind of ironic that the Sarawak government should challenge the PDA when two of the state’s most prominent “sons” had informed Parliament in 1974 that the state had agreed to the legislation, considered to be “of national interest”.
Be that as it may, the parties before the Federal Court will lock horns in a battle for legal clarity and constitutionality in January 2027.
Let the legal battle take its course.

15d77d649ee9df89: ISTANBUL, Oct 14 — Barcelona and Lamine Yamal rediscovered their sparkle after a rocky first-half spell in the cauldron of Istanbul’s Ali Sami Yen stadium to win 4-1 away to Galatasaray in the Champions League yesterday.
Yamal tore the hosts apart after half time.
“It’s incredible to have players like that,” said Barcelona coach Hansi Flick. “He’s turned the game around for us.”
Halfway through the second round of matches, the victory lifted Barcelona to the top of the Champions League table with two wins. Galatasaray are pointless and near the foot of the standings.
“We’re at a very high level. We have to keep going; the season is very long. We can’t relax,” Barcelona’s Fermin Lopez told Spanish broadcaster Movistar.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal controls the ball during their Champions League match against Galatasaray at the Ali Sami Yen Sports Complex in Istanbul on October 13, 2026. — AFP pic
Barcelona dominated the early stages. With Yamal vigorously policed on the right by the home defence, many of their attacks flowed through Anthony Gordon on the other flank.
Yet Galatasaray took the lead after 27 minutes. After Gordon went tumbling in the penalty box, the hosts launched a rapid counter-attack through Rafael Leao on the left.
He pulled the ball back to the edge of the area to Russian Aleksei Batrakov whose drive deflected off Joao Cancelo and into the corner of the goal.
“That goal made things a bit strange for us, because we had been dominating. But we knew how to react and come back,” said Fermin.
That ignited a spell of furious home pressure which culminated with Victor Osimhen rising to head a corner past goalkeeper Joan Garcia. Baris Yilmaz toed the ball over the line but was ruled offside.

Barcelona reasserted control. When Yamal went down on the edge of the box, the ball broke to a surprised Davinson Sanchez who gave the ball away immediately. It fell to Dani Olmo who threaded a pass to Cancelo who scored.

At the start of the second half Yamal took over. After setting up Gordon, who spurned the chance, he helped put Barca ahead in the 50th minute, placing a gentle curled cross on the forehead of Fermin who nodded home.

“He’s a friend and a great team-mate,” said Fermin of Yamal. “When he has the ball, I always look for a run. He’s the best in the world. We get along well off the field, and that shows on the pitch, too.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Barcelona’s Fermin Lopez celebrates scoring his team’s second goal against Galatasaray during their Champions League match in Istanbul on October 13, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Everyone’s watching Lamine’
Three minutes later, Yamal beat Eren Elmali three times, and in three different ways, in a tiny space before rolling a pass to Gordon in front of goal.
This time the England striker made no mistake with Elmali, a Turkey international, lifting his arms to the heavens in an expression of powerlessness.

After 65 minutes Yamal cut in from his wing and fired a pass to replacement centre forward Gabriel Jesus. The ex-Arsenal man could not control the ball but it deflected to Karim Adeyemi who drilled the ball home.
“When you see the chances Lamine creates in every training session, it’s the same in matches,” said Flick. “I have a lot of top-quality players. Everyone’s watching Lamine - that’s only natural.”
Yamal could have scored himself but after being quickest to a loose ball he fired his shot over the bar.

The 19-year-old finished the game without a goal which would have taken him closer to Kylian Mbappe’s record for Champions League goals as a teenager, but Yamal, who became Barcelona’s youngest ever captain in the previous round, again took over the captain’s armband when Pedri was replaced. — AFP

7abf873b6857248b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Air quality deteriorated further across the country this morning, with 27 monitoring stations recording unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings as haze intensified across the central and southern regions of Peninsular Malaysia.

According to Department of Environment (DOE) surveillance data as of 8.54am, 27 out of the nation’s 68 stations registered readings in the unhealthy bracket (API 101 to 200), marking a noticeable increase from the 20 stations reported yesterday morning.
Another 40 stations logged moderate air quality, only one recorded good air quality, and none crossed into the very unhealthy or hazardous categories.

Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded the country's highest reading at 177, easing marginally from 181 yesterday morning. Nilai in Negeri Sembilan saw a sharp overnight spike, jumping from 151 to 174, while Klang and peat fire hotspot Johan Setia in Selangor were tied close behind at 173.
Selangor accounted for five unhealthy stations. Beyond Klang and Johan Setia, elevated readings were recorded in Banting (160), Shah Alam (159), and Petaling Jaya (154).

In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras logged 168 and Batu Muda stood at 164. The administrative centre of Putrajaya rebounded sharply into the unhealthy bracket at 165, up from 120 yesterday morning, breaching the 150-point benchmark used for localized school closure assessments.
Southern and eastern states record rising smoke levels

Johor saw the highest concentration of polluted areas nationwide, with seven stations in the unhealthy band. Following Pasir Gudang, elevated readings were registered in Kota Tinggi (166), Larkin (164), Pengerang (162), Batu Pahat (154), Kluang (152), and Tangkak (151).
In Negeri Sembilan, coastal Port Dickson re-entered the unhealthy register at 165 after dropping out yesterday, while state capital Seremban climbed to 160.
All three monitoring stations in Melaka worsened overnight: Bukit Rambai rose to 169, Bandaraya Melaka stood at 164, and Alor Gajah recorded 156.

On the East Coast, smoke pollution rebounded in Terengganu, with industrial hubs Kemaman and Paka logging 156 and 155 respectively after exiting the list yesterday. In Pahang, Indera Mahkota in Kuantan recorded 155 and Rompin registered 153.
In Sarawak, Serian logged an unhealthy reading of 153, while Sri Aman improved significantly, easing from 170 yesterday to 134 to mark the lowest reading among the 27 affected stations.
Widespread school closures remain in effect
The worsening air quality comes as schools in multiple states remained shut today.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek confirmed that all primary and secondary schools across Johor, Melaka, and Negeri Sembilan would stay closed today.

Targeted shutdowns also remain in effect for schools under nine District Education Offices (PPD) nationwide: Hulu Langat and Sepang in Selangor; Kuantan, Pekan, and Rompin in Pahang; Tawau in Sabah; alongside Serian, Sri Aman, and Lubok Antu in Sarawak.

Health and education authorities have urged parents, high-risk groups, and students with respiratory ailments to wear protective face masks outdoors and track real-time hourly API updates via official DOE portals.

80d042ecc4ef0613: LOS ANGELES, Oct 14 — Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former Los Angeles gang leader who boasted for years of his involvement in the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, only to deny it when he came to trial, was sentenced to a minimum 40 years in prison on Tuesday.

The sentence, which will likely see him die in custody, comes three decades after the gunning down of one of the most influential hip hop artists of the late 20th century, and after years of criticism over investigations that went nowhere.
Davis, 63, formerly ran a branch of the feared Crips, one of a patchwork of rival gangs that controlled parts of Los Angeles in the 1990s.
He spent years evading justice and seemingly believed he was beyond the reach of the law when he wrote in his memoir that he had ordered the killing of Shakur.

“For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing to law enforcement... in your book, and it’s something like, ‘Yeah, I was involved in this, but I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,’” Judge Carli Kierny told Davis as she handed down the sentence in a Las Vegas courtroom.
“I’m here to tell you that’s not how this works.”
“You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur,” the judge said.
Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas.
A trial heard how Davis ordered the September 7, 1996 killing of the hip-hop artist after his own nephew had been beaten by members of Shakur’s entourage at a Las Vegas casino.
The “California Love” artist was shot about two hours after the casino confrontation by a gunman in a white Cadillac that pulled up at a red light alongside the BMW in which the rapper was riding.
Davis handed the gun to someone sitting in the back seat of the Cadillac and ordered that person to shoot Shakur, who died six days later.
The name of that person has not been definitively revealed and Davis is the only person who was in the Cadillac that evening who is still alive.
The driver of the BMW, Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight, was wounded.
‘Born an icon’
The killing of Shakur, also known as 2Pac, was one of America’s most famous cold cases, prompting endless debate among music fans over who did it, and why.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A 1996 photo of rapper Tupac Shukur (left) and Marion ‘Suge’ Knight is displayed during the Duane Davis murder trial, related to the 1996 killing of the rapper, in Las Vegas August 17, 2026. — AFP pic

Known for hits including “All Eyez on Me,” Shakur — the son of a Black Panther activist — was raised in Harlem and Baltimore, but quickly became the epitome of California hip hop when he signed with Los Angeles-based Death Row Records.
His sister Sekyiwa Shakur paid emotional tribute on Tuesday to her brother, a man whom she said “was born an icon.”

She said their mother “consciously raised him to be a human rights activist, someone to stand up for those weaker and smaller than he was, and that’s who he was to me and all the family. He was the person that you go to for protection.

“He dedicated his career to the advancement of his people. He was gentle and kind to women and children. He fed anyone he knew that didn’t have. He was truly my shining star, my shining prince. He was who God trusted to take care of me.”
Davis offered no words of contrition ahead of the sentence being handed down, vowing only to appeal the guilty finding. — AFP

c48596c03ec817ff: SAN FRANCISCO: A Saudi employee of OpenAI was arrested after allegedly planting a recording device in one of the company's San Francisco offices, the AI firm and federal prosecutors said Tuesday.
"We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices" and "referred the matter to the FBI," OpenAI told AFP in a statement.
OpenAI's security team found the device late last month and the employee, Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested on Oct 9, the US justice department said.

Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer who had worked for OpenAI since July 2025, allegedly wrapped a USB device in toilet paper and inserted it into a television located in an "executive conference room," according to a justice department statement.
He was allegedly caught on camera "near" the conference room multiple times but was not authorised to participate in meetings located there.
He used a "productivity tool" to search for more information about OpenAI's office buildings, meeting rooms, calendars, schedules and people's locations, according to the statement.
A chatbot account connected to Alfozan's spouse also allegedly contained queries related to remote audio recording and encrypting memory cards.
"This serious situation underscores why winning the global super intelligence race is a national security prerogative," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said in the statement.
"The intelligence community remains committed to safeguarding America's cutting-edge intellectual property from foreign threats," Clayton added.
The arrest and allegations come amid a fierce global race to dominate in artificial intelligence, which the Trump administration has pushed to be rebranded as "superintelligence."
Saudi Arabia's state-backed AI firm Humain invested US$3 billion in Elon Musk's xAI shortly before the American billionaire's space company, SpaceX, acquired the AI division in February.
Now known as SpaceXAI, the division announced last year that it was teaming up with Humain to build a 500-megawatt data centre in Saudi Arabia.
Multiple devices
It was not immediately clear what, if any information the recording device was able to collect.
"At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," OpenAI told AFP in a statement.
A second device was found by OpenAI's security team when they searched an unattended bag that belonged to Alfozan, according to the justice department.
Alfozan was caught on security footage from inside the restricted conference room where he appeared to look behind the television where the recording device had been placed, the department said.
A LinkedIn account matching Alfozan's name and resume show that he previously worked at Facebook-owner Meta, as well as an AI startup and a venture capital firm.
He was also a student at University of California at Berkeley and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

The justice department said Alfozan had been charged with "using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications," for which he could face up to five years in prison and a US$250,000 fine.
It did not accuse Alfozan nor Saudi Arabia, which is a close US ally, of spying activity in its statement on Tuesday.
Alfozan is expected to appear at a federal court hearing on Oct 19.
In 2022, a former Twitter worker, Ahmad Abouammo, was found guilty of spying for Saudi officials keen to unmask critics on the platform.

f00140b0f6a5c9c9: DUBLIN: Microsoft president Brad Smith warned Tuesday that industry and governments must "act with urgency" to create "real and effective safety standards" to contain the risks linked to artificial intelligence.

"We're going to need for AI what we have for everything else in life... we need real and effective safety standards, and we need the public to have confidence in them," Smith told a group of reporters on the eve of an international AI summit in Dublin.
Concerns about AI safety have soared in recent months after models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in security incidents during testing, piling on pressure to regulate the technology.

"We've reached a point where we obviously need companies in the industry to step up and do more to address AI safety issues," Smith said. "I think we reached a time when we're going to need governments to do more as well."

The Microsoft boss outlined the company's proposals to strengthen safety across the sector, starting with a requirement that AI agents be equipped with "safety brakes" that users could activate in the event of an incident.
"The notion, especially for any AI that's running on critical infrastructure or some other kind of automated system, they have the ability to turn off or slow down," he explained.
Smith also called for AI providers to face mandatory incident-reporting obligations.

"If you are a business and you suffer a security breach that leads to the loss of consumer data, you have to let consumers know," he said. "The same logic should apply to people harmed by an AI agent," with a legal obligation to inform those affected.
The Microsoft president further advocated stronger testing and evaluation of AI models before they are released, to ensure they are safe.
"We need to act with urgency," he warned.

Smith is the latest in a series of leading industry figures to highlight the need for increased vigilance around AI technology. Among them, Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, has pledged to slow development unilaterally if necessary.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Tuesday said AI company leaders must take responsibility for ensuring the technology is developed safely.
Speaking in Paris, Huang said: "The full potential of AI can only be realised if we advance the capabilities of AI and the safety and security of AI at the same time."
"These are not conflicting goals. These are, in fact, the same goal."

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the proposal could be considered by examining data on about 225,000 people with refugee status, based on records maintained by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
He said the government intended to identify refugees of working age who had passed screening to assess their potential to meet the country's workforce needs.
"On the other hand, we have 225,000 people whom UNHCR recognises as refugees. They are right here in front of us. This is a big idea, but it has not been implemented yet.
"If we could compile data on these 225,000 people and identify those within the productive age range, such as 20, 25 or 30, who have been screened, we would have the data.
"Our intention is to meet workforce needs without necessarily recruiting from abroad.

"For example, if an oil palm plantation in Pasir Gudang needs 100 workers, there are two options. We could recruit workers from Bangladesh and pay all the associated costs, or check our existing refugee registration database.
"For now, I am not ruling out the possibility of taking this route to meet the actual workforce needs we face," he said in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.

He was responding to Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau), who sought clarification on whether the government planned to allow Rohingya refugees registered under the Refugee Documentation Programme (DPP) to work in the 3D sectors, particularly amid a shortage of foreign workers.
Saifuddin said foreign worker requirements were currently concentrated in five economic sectors, namely manufacturing, plantations, agriculture, construction and services.
He said labour shortages in these sectors could affect economic activities, particularly jobs such as harvesting oil palm fresh fruit bunches and laying bricks.
"There are five economic sectors that require workers. The Economy Ministry has set a ceiling on the number of foreign workers who can be brought in.

"Under the 13th Malaysia Plan, the number must not exceed 10 per cent of the workforce. Our workforce stands at 17 million, meaning the ceiling is 1.7 million throughout the 13th Malaysia Plan for the five economic sectors.
"If these five sectors do not have foreign workers, our economy will be affected. That means there would be no one to harvest oil palm or lay bricks. That is the reality.
"Every year, the Home Ministry is among the regulatory agencies involved in decisions on approvals for foreign workers and related matters," he said.
a333cdd21cedddd6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) denied reports in a local newspaper and on social media claiming a Malaysian university student was arrested for smuggling over four kilogrammes of syabu in Tanjung Balai, Indonesia, on October 10.

Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations found that the suspect arrested by the republic’s authorities is a 21-year-old Indonesian man.
He said the suspect, from Medan, is a student at a higher learning institution in Indonesia.
Hussein said the drugs were obtained from a syndicate in Malaysia before being smuggled out.

“Further investigations revealed the drugs were handed over by another Indonesian man in the Klang Valley to be brought to Indonesia via the Tanjung Balai Ferry Terminal,” he said in a statement yesterday.

The suspect was arrested by Tanjung Balai Police (POLRES) at 5pm local time on October 10 after arriving at the Teluk Nibung Ferry Terminal in Tanjung Balai on a ferry from Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan.
Hussein said an X-ray scan of the man’s luggage found eight plastic packets suspected to contain methamphetamine, weighing 4.044 kilogrammes.
He stressed that the report titled “Lagi kes rakyat Malaysia ditahan, pelajar universiti ‘kantoi’ seludup 4kg syabu” is untrue and could cause confusion and concern among the public.
“NCID urges relevant parties not to spread any news without verified facts and to obtain prior confirmation from the authorities,” he said.
He said NCID takes cross-border smuggling seriously and will continue to cooperate with the Indonesian National Police (POLRI).
He said the cooperation aims to gather intelligence to identify the supply source and dismantle drug syndicate networks in Malaysia linked to the case.
The public with information on the case is urged to channel it through the NCID hotline at 012-208 7222. — Bernama
5dd6dec51f64af4f: KUALA LUMPUR: They may be tiny, colourful and look a little like caviar, but fish eggs found on sushi are not necessarily considered a luxury delicacy under the law.

The High Court has ruled that tobiko (flying fish roe), masago (capelin roe) and frozen mentaiko (pollock roe) imported by restaurant chain Sushi King Sdn Bhd are not caviar substitutes, despite being seasoned, coloured and preserved.

Judge Norliza Othman ruled this when dismissing an appeal by the Customs Department director-general against a Customs Appeal Tribunal decision in favour of Sushi King over the classification of the three products.
The dispute centred on whether the fish eggs should be classified as caviar substitutes, which attract an 8 per cent import duty, or other prepared or preserved fish, which carry zero import duty.
On Oct 8, 2020, Sushi King submitted three applications to the Customs Department seeking tariff rulings for the imported fish roe.
The department classified the products as caviar substitutes, which attract an 8 per cent import duty.
Dissatisfied with the classification, Sushi King sought a review and proposed different tariff codes for the three products. However, Customs maintained its decision on Dec 7, 2021.
Sushi King then appealed to the Customs Appeal Tribunal, which ruled in its favour on Dec 1, 2023, and set aside the department's classification.
This prompted the Customs Department director-general to challenge the tribunal's decision in the High Court.
In its appeal, Customs argued that the products qualified as caviar substitutes because they had undergone several processes, including cleaning, seasoning, colouring and freezing.
It maintained that the processing methods and fish egg content met the requirements for caviar substitutes under the Customs Duties Order 2017.
Customs also argued that how the products were consumed should not determine whether they qualified as caviar substitutes.
However, Sushi King maintained that the products were commonly used as toppings or garnishes in Japanese cuisine and were neither consumed nor marketed as alternatives to caviar.
The company argued that not all processed or seasoned fish eggs could automatically be classified as caviar substitutes.

In her judgment, Norliza agreed with Sushi King, saying that not all fish eggs could be considered caviar substitutes and that how they were consumed was an important factor in determining their classification.
"Fish roe is a wide, all-encompassing term used to describe fish eggs, but not all fish roe is caviar or a caviar substitute.

"In this regard, caviar substitute is a very specific subset of fish roe based on its origin, methods of consumption and method of processing, which aims to mimic sturgeon caviar," she said in her grounds of judgment published by the Judiciary Department yesterday.
Norliza said Sushi King's imported products were used as toppings or garnishes in Japanese cuisine rather than being marketed as alternatives to caviar.
She said the World Customs Organisation's explanatory notes described caviar substitutes as products made from the eggs of fish other than sturgeon, which were prepared and consumed as caviar.
The judge said imported goods must be classified according to the relevant legal provisions and the WCO's guidelines.
She also found that the Customs Appeal Tribunal had carefully examined the products, including their composition, preparation methods and how they were consumed, before ruling in Sushi King's favour.
Senior federal counsel Nur Aishah Maulat Ahmad Zakiuddin and federal counsel Muhaimin Mohamed represented the appellant, while S. Saravana Kumar and Darshini Sharma appeared for Sushi King.

d854ce6a0f0c00e7: PETALING JAYA: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) is targeting several parliamentary seats held by its rivals in the next general election, but analysts says its ambitions may hinge on electoral pacts and its ability to retain its existing seats.
GRS secretary-general Armizan Mohd Ali said last Tuesday that a simulation based on the results of the 2025 Sabah state election suggested the coalition could win more than 15 parliamentary seats.
GRS won six out of Sabah’s 25 parliamentary seats in the 15th general election (GE15): Papar, Sipitang, Ranau, Keningau, Batu Sapi and Tawau.

Universiti Malaya’s political analyst Awang Azman Pawi said GRS had reason to be optimistic following a strong showing in the state polls, which demonstrated broad support across rural, interior and west coast areas.
“Upko’s entry into GRS has also further expanded the coalition’s support base, especially among Kadazandusun-Murut voters and in mixed constituencies,” he told FMT.
Key battlegrounds
Awang Azman identified Kudat, Kota Belud, Beaufort, Kimanis, Beluran and Kota Marudu — constituencies not currently held by the coalition — as key battlegrounds in GRS’s push for expansion.
Kudat appears promising, he said, noting that GRS won in Banggi, Pitas and Tanjong Kapor, three of the four state seats within the parliamentary constituency at the recent state polls.
The parliamentary seat is currently held by independent assemblyman Verdon Bahanda, who, two months ago indicated he was “seriously considering” an offer to join Barisan Nasional.

Kota Belud, a Warisan seat, could also become more interesting following Upko’s entry into GRS. The coalition could potentially combine its strength in Tempasuk with Upko’s influence in Kadamaian. Warisan holds the third state seat, Usukan, while Pintasan is represented by an independent assemblyman.
Beaufort, currently held by BN, is another potential target with GRS having won both state seats within the constituency — Klias and Kuala Penyu — in the 2025 state election.
GRS also holds all three state seats within Beluran — Telupid, Sugut and Labuk — giving it a potential advantage in its bid to wrest the parliamentary seat from Perikatan Nasional.
In Kota Marudu — presently held by Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) — GRS holds Matunggong and Tandek, while Bandau is represented by an independent assemblyman.
In Kimanis, presently held by BN, GRS controls the state seat of Membakut, while Warisan holds Bongawan.
Tougher challenge elsewhere
Kinabatangan and Libaran — both BN strongholds — could be considered second-tier targets, Awang Azman said, but GRS would need strong candidates and a favourable landscape to wrest them away.
Within Kinabatangan, GRS holds the Kuamut state seat, while BN controls the Lamag and Sukau seats.
In Libaran, GRS holds Sungai Manila, while Warisan holds Gum Gum and Sungai Sibuga.

Awang Azman cautioned, however, that GRS’s immediate priority should be defending its existing parliamentary seats — especially Ranau, Sipitang, Batu Sapi and Tawau — which may not be safe in a general election given the differences between state and parliamentary voting patterns.
Strategic cooperation

Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s Bilcher Bala said the seven parliamentary seats held by BN and the five held by Pakatan Harapan, both partners in the GRS-led state government, posed a strategic dilemma for GRS.

He said electoral cooperation with both coalitions could increase the number of parliamentary seats won by the state government bloc, but warned it could also limit the number of seats GRS itself could contest and win.
Bilcher said a target of 10 to 12 seats under its own banner would be more attainable if GRS agrees to seat-sharing arrangements with BN and PH.

“To reach 15 seats, however, GRS would need either to contest and win several BN and PH seats or secure an agreement for its allies to contest under a common political umbrella, allowing their victories to be counted as GRS-led bloc victories,” he said.

According to Bilcher, the first option risks splitting votes and benefiting Warisan, STAR, KDM or independent candidates, while the second would require extensive negotiations over leadership and seat allocation.
Bilcher said GRS’s target should therefore be assessed not only by the number of seats it wins directly, but also by the strength of the broader state government bloc.
He also identified Tenom and Putatan as potential battlegrounds.
GRS won Kemabong, one of the two state seats under Tenom, while in Putatan it won Tanjung Keramat, with Warisan holding Tanjung Aru, and Petagas represented by an independent assemblyman.
3d29d49b0b86e68b: PETALING JAYA: Malaysian cuisine is often introduced to the world through nasi lemak and roti canai. Yet those familiar favourites only scratch the surface of the country’s rich culinary landscape.
One Malaysian-born couple, now living in Australia, hopes to showcase Malaysia’s lesser-known flavours.
Geetha Ganesan and her husband, Nithyaraj Subramaniam, run MalayaLane, claiming it is Adelaide’s first Malaysian-Indian cuisine restaurant.
The couple first started with a commercial kitchen and a takeaway business called Smatra Curry House.
Geetha, from Kulai, Johor, worked as a banker in Malaysia, while Nithyaraj, from Ipoh, had some F&B experience. For Geetha, however, cooking has always been a part of her life.

“I started cooking when I was about 12 because I’m the eldest of my siblings, so I cooked for my younger brothers and sisters. My grandmothers taught me, and it became second nature to me,” she told FMT Lifestyle.

Nithyaraj moved to Australia for a job in 2018, and Geetha joined him after they married in 2022. The couple spent two years in Melbourne before relocating to Adelaide, South Australia. There, they missed the flavours of home.
“South Indian and North Indian food was already quite common, but we couldn’t find any Malaysian Indian food in Adelaide,” said Geetha. “We are the first to bring that taste here.”
The couple registered Smatra Curry House and began promoting their food through Malaysian community groups.
Focusing on home-style Indian food was not initially the plan.
Geetha started with pandan nasi lemak, and customers soon began asking for banana leaf rice, prompting the couple to add it as a takeaway option. They received 35 orders right away.
This venture connected the couple with Malaysians in the city. Some had been living in Adelaide for 10 or 20 years, occasionally travelling all the way to Melbourne for authentic Malaysian food.
“People would tell me, ‘Your food tastes like home.’ Sometimes I have even seen our customers cry in front of us after eating because they missed that kind of food,” she said.
As word spread, the business expanded into pop-ups, food carnivals and expos, where the couple sold Malaysian favourites including Ramly burger, nasi vanggey and Roti John.
“At one point, every corner of my car was filled with packs of food - there was no space left. We knew then that it was time to open a restaurant,” Geetha recalled.
Smatra Curry House was rebranded as MalayaLane and officially opened on April 11.

Despite being 30km from the city centre, MalayaLane drew strong support on its first day, with a queue stretching around the premises. In fact, Jing Lee, the first Malaysian-born member of the South Australian Parliament, attended the grand opening.
“The crowd was much bigger than we expected - around 170 customers showed up. At one point we ran out of rice, but people were still willing to wait,” Geetha said.
Today, MalayaLane’s weekday lunch menu, its busiest period, features staples such as pandan nasi lemak with fried chicken, mee goreng, laksa and more.
On weekends, the menu expands to include banana leaf rice, served with a spread of 13 accompaniments including three vegetables along with curries, raita, papadum and dessert.
Diners can also add dishes such as Chicken 65, sardine sambal cili padi and fish head curry.

“I tell all our customers, ‘Whether you are Malaysian or not, you should enjoy the banana leaf meal with your hands,’” said Geetha. “I even teach them to crush the papadum into the payasam on the leaf itself - that’s how we would eat back home.”
The weekend menu also features ghee rice with chicken sambal or lamb masala, nasi kandar, and Ipoh-style nasi ganja.
With a Royal Australian Air Force base nearby, former personnel who trained in Butterworth decades ago also drop by MalayaLane, reminiscing about their time in Malaysia and the food they remember.
For now, Geetha and Nithyaraj are focused on MalayaLane, but hope to open two more branches in the future. “We want to show people that this is also Malaysian food.”
Follow MalayaLane on Instagram and Facebook.
f27a4ddefa061ddc: PETALING JAYA: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) menyasarkan beberapa kerusi Parlimen yang dikuasai lawannya pada PRU akan datang, namun penganalisis berkata hasrat itu mungkin bergantung pada pakatan pilihan raya dan keupayaan mempertahankan kerusi sedia ada.
Selasa lalu, Setiausaha Agung GRS, Armizan Mohd Ali, berkata simulasi berdasarkan keputusan PRN Sabah 2025 menunjukkan gabungan itu berpotensi memenangi lebih daripada 15 kerusi Parlimen.
GRS menang enam daripada 25 kerusi Parlimen Sabah pada PRU15 iaitu Papar, Sipitang, Ranau, Keningau, Batu Sapi dan Tawau.

Penganalisis politik daripada Universiti Malaya, Awang Azman Pawi, berkata GRS mempunyai alasan untuk optimis susulan prestasi cemerlang dalam PRN, yang menunjukkan sokongan meluas di kawasan luar bandar, pedalaman dan pantai barat.
“Kemasukan Upko ke dalam GRS turut meluaskan lagi asas sokongan gabungan itu, khususnya dalam kalangan pengundi Kadazandusun-Murut dan di kawasan campuran,” katanya kepada FMT.
Medan pertempuran utama
Awang Azman mengenal pasti Kudat, Kota Belud, Beaufort, Kimanis, Beluran dan Kota Marudu — kawasan Parlimen milik lawan — sebagai medan pertempuran utama dalam usaha GRS meluaskan penguasaannya.
Kudat dilihat berpotensi, katanya, sambil menyatakan GRS memenangi Banggi, Pitas dan Tanjong Kapor, iaitu tiga daripada empat kerusi DUN dalam kawasan Parlimen itu pada PRN baru-baru ini.
Kerusi Parlimen itu kini disandang wakil rakyat bebas, Verdon Bahanda, yang dua bulan lalu menyatakan 'sedang mempertimbangkan dengan serius' tawaran untuk menyertai Barisan Nasional (BN).

Kota Belud, yang merupakan kerusi Warisan, juga berpotensi menjadi lebih menarik susulan penyertaan Upko dalam GRS. Gabungan itu berpotensi menggabungkan kekuatannya di Tempasuk dengan pengaruh Upko di Kadamaian. Warisan menguasai kerusi DUN ketiga, Usukan, manakala Pintasan diwakili seorang wakil rakyat bebas.
Beaufort, yang kini disandang oleh BN, merupakan satu lagi sasaran berpotensi apabila GRS memenangi kedua-dua kerusi DUN dalam kawasan Parlimen itu, iaitu Klias dan Kuala Penyu, pada PRN 2025.
GRS turut menguasai ketiga-tiga DUN dalam kawasan Beluran — Telupid, Sugut dan Labuk — sekali gus memberikan kelebihan dalam usahanya merampas kerusi Parlimen itu daripada Perikatan Nasional (PN).
Di Kota Marudu, yang kini disandang oleh Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM), GRS menguasai Matunggong dan Tandek, manakala Bandau diwakili oleh seorang wakil rakyat bebas.
Di Kimanis, yang kini disandang oleh BN, GRS menguasai kerusi DUN Membakut, manakala Warisan menguasai Bongawan.
Cabaran lebih sukar di kawasan lain

Kinabatangan dan Libaran — kedua-duanya kubu kuat BN — boleh dianggap sebagai sasaran peringkat kedua, kata Awang Azman, tetapi GRS memerlukan calon yang kuat dan landskap politik yang memihak kepadanya untuk merampas kedua-dua kerusi itu.
Di Kinabatangan, GRS menguasai kerusi DUN Kuamut, manakala BN menguasai kerusi Lamag dan Sukau.
Di Libaran, GRS menguasai Sungai Manila, manakala Warisan menguasai Gum Gum dan Sungai Sibuga.

Bagaimanapun, Awang Azman mengingatkan keutamaan GRS sepatutnya ialah mempertahankan Parlimen sedia ada — khususnya Ranau, Sipitang, Batu Sapi dan Tawau — yang mungkin tidak selamat memandangkan perbezaan corak pengundian antara PRN dengan PRU.
Kerjasama strategik

Bilcher Bala daripada Universiti Malaysia Sabah berkata, tujuh kerusi Parlimen disandang BN dan lima disandang PH, yang kedua-duanya merupakan rakan dalam kerajaan negeri pimpinan GRS, menimbulkan dilema strategik bagi GRS.

Beliau berkata, kerjasama pilihan raya dengan kedua-dua gabungan itu boleh meningkatkan jumlah kerusi Parlimen dimenangi blok kerajaan negeri, tetapi memberi amaran langkah itu juga boleh mengehadkan jumlah kerusi yang boleh ditandingi dan dimenangi oleh GRS sendiri.
Katanya, sasaran 10 hingga 12 kerusi atas tiket sendiri lebih mudah dicapai jika GRS bersetuju dengan aturan pembahagian kerusi bersama BN dan PH.

“Bagaimanapun, untuk mencapai 15 kerusi, GRS perlu sama ada bertanding dan memenangi beberapa kerusi BN dan PH atau mendapatkan persetujuan supaya sekutunya bertanding bawah satu payung politik, sekali gus membolehkan kemenangan mereka dikira sebagai kemenangan blok pimpinan GRS,” katanya.

Menurut Bilcher, pilihan pertama berisiko memecahkan undi dan memberi kelebihan kepada Warisan, STAR, KDM atau calon bebas, manakala pilihan kedua memerlukan rundingan yang meluas berhubung kepimpinan dan pembahagian kerusi.
Bilcher berkata, justeru sasaran GRS perlu dinilai bukan sahaja berdasarkan jumlah kerusi dimenanginya secara langsung, tetapi kekuatan blok kerajaan negeri yang lebih luas.
Beliau turut mengenal pasti Tenom dan Putatan sebagai medan pertempuran yang bepotensi dimenangi.

GRS memenangi Kemabong, satu daripada dua DUN bawah Parlimen Tenom, manakala di Putatan, GRS menang Tanjung Keramat, Warisan pula menguasai Tanjung Aru dan Petagas diwakili seorang wakil rakyat bebas.
45072a7087a0d8f6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — A total of 52,133 owners of diesel vehicles such as pickups and sport utility vehicles (SUVs) in Sabah have been approved for an additional 100 litres of diesel under the Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) programme as of October 12, 2026, said the Ministry of Finance (MoF).

The ministry said the additional eligibility criteria take into account the higher diesel consumption needs, particularly among rural residents, small traders, farmers and those who use diesel vehicles to generate income.
In addition, a total of 19,008 Budi Diesel eligibility transfer applications have been approved, with 5,555 of them involving applicants from Sabah.
MoF noted that the government implemented the diesel subsidy targeting reform through Budi Diesel in phases beginning June 27, 2026, before expanding its implementation nationwide on July 1, 2026.

The ministry said this in response to a question from Vivian Wong Shir Yee (Sandakan-PH) regarding the diesel subsidy mechanism in Sabah in a written answer published on the Parliament’s website yesterday.

For users other than individual vehicle owners, MoF said the government also considers the needs of certain groups that rely on diesel for daily use, including boat operators as well as users of electric generators (gensets) and water pumps in rural areas.

It pointed out that these groups could be considered for Budi Diesel assistance through the MyKad mechanism, subject to eligibility requirements and verification by the state government and relevant agencies, such as district offices, resident offices or designated state agencies.
The measure aims to ensure that groups that truly rely on diesel to meet their daily needs do not miss out on receiving assistance.
“The government will continue to monitor the implementation of BUDI Diesel based on usage data, user feedback, input from the state government and the needs of the sectors involved.

“Any improvements will be refined through data so that diesel subsidies can be channelled more easily, fairly, in a more targeted and sustainable manner to users who truly qualify, without opening up opportunities for leakage or abuse of subsidies,” MoF added. — Bernama
adabe8b988ef54df: ROME, Oct 14 — Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous tumour removed from his right lung in a 90-minute operation yesterday and “woke up normally” after the procedure, the Vatican said.
A Vatican source said further tests were being carried out to determine if the cancer had spread.
“To ensure the procedure was radical, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed,” the Vatican said in a statement.
The operation “confirmed the diagnosis of a pulmonary adenocarcinoma, as suspected from the pre-operative tests”, it said.
The 71-year-old pope was in the operating room at Rome’s Gemelli hospital for a total of three hours and the operation lasted half that time.
“The surgery was successful and there were no complications,” the Vatican said, with a source adding that he had requested dinner after the procedure.
Juanita Mora, medical spokesperson for the American Lung Association, told AFP that when this type of cancer is “caught in early stages, then it has a very, very good prognosis”.
She said much would depend on the stage of the cancer found and whether it had spread.
In cases of surgical removal and when the cancer is caught early and localised, five-year survival rates from lung adenocarcinoma were “80 to 98 per cent”, she said.
“They’ll determine if he needs chemotherapy, radiation therapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy for the adenocarcinoma,” she said.
